enonce.texte:
Listen to the words and choose the correct one you hear. Focus on difficult sounds for French speakers: /θ/ vs /t/, /ð/ vs /d/, and /r/ vs /l/.

1. A) Think B) Tink

2. A) Then B) Den

3. A) Right B) Light

4. A) Three B) Tree

5. A) Breathe B) Breed

questions.texte: Select the correct word based on pronunciation.
questions.reponse: 1. A, 2. A, 3. A, 4. A, 5. A (or B depending on audio)

enonce.texte:
Identify the stressed syllable in each word by writing the syllable number (1, 2, 3, etc.).

1. TEACHER → _______

2. COMPUTER → _______

3. UNDERSTAND → _______

4. BEAUTIFUL → _______

5. DEVELOP → _______

questions.texte: Identify the stressed syllable in each word.

enonce.texte:
Rewrite the sentences as they would be pronounced in natural connected speech using linking (consonant-vowel linking).

1. "I am going to see him." → _______

2. "She is a teacher." → _______

3. "They are at the office." → _______

4. "We have a meeting." → _______

5. "He is not here." → _______

questions.reponse: 1. "I'm gonna see him." or "I am going to see him." with linking: "I‿am‿going‿to‿see‿him." 2. "She‿is‿a teacher." 3. "They‿are‿at‿the‿office." 4. "We‿have‿a meeting." 5. "He‿is‿not‿here."

enonce.texte:
Identify which sounds are elided (dropped) in natural speech.

1. "I don't know" → /aɪ doʊnt noʊ/ - What is elided? _______

2. "She wants to go" → /ʃi wɒnts tə goʊ/ - What is elided? _______

3. "I want to see you" → /aɪ wɒn tə si ju/ - What is elided? _______

4. "They asked me" → /ðeɪ ɑːskt mi/ - What is elided? _______

5. "I had to go" → /aɪ hæd tə goʊ/ - What is elided? _______

questions.texte: Identify the elided sound in each phrase.
questions.reponse: 1. The /t/ in "don't" is elided. 2. The /t/ in "wants" is elided. 3. The /t/ in "want" is elided. 4. The /k/ in "asked" is elided. 5. The /v/ in "had" is elided (or the /d/ is softened).

enonce.texte:
Compare the French-influenced pronunciation with the correct English pronunciation. Write the correct English pronunciation.

1. French: /ʒə/ for "yes" → English: _______

2. French: /pɔr/ for "poor" → English: _______

3. French: /ɛkɔl/ for "school" → English: _______

4. French: /ʃɛr/ for "chair" → English: _______

5. French: /z/ for the "th" sound → English: _______

questions.texte: Write the correct English pronunciation for each word.

enonce.texte:
Identify which words are stressed in each sentence. Underline the stressed content words (nouns, main verbs, adjectives, adverbs).

1. "I want to go to the market."

2. "She is a very good teacher."

3. "They are coming to the party."

4. "We need to finish the project."

5. "He can speak four languages."

questions.reponse: 1. I <u>want</u> to <u>go</u> to the <u>market</u>. 2. She is a <u>very</u> <u>good</u> <u>teacher</u>. 3. They are <u>coming</u> to the <u>party</u>. 4. We <u>need</u> to <u>finish</u> the <u>project</u>. 5. He can <u>speak</u> <u>four</u> <u>languages</u>.

enonce.texte:
Record yourself saying these sentences. Then listen and identify areas for improvement.

1. "I think three things are important."

2. "She works with her brother."

3. "Please pass the rice and the light."

4. "They are going to meet at the library."

5. "I would like to have a nice car."

questions.texte: Evaluate your pronunciation and identify 3 areas for improvement.
questions.reponse:
Example answer: 
1. I need to practice the /θ/ sound in "think" and "three".
2. I should work on linking in "She works with her brother".
3. I need to distinguish /r/ and /l/ in "rice" and "light".

enonce.texte:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence. Focus on the minimal pair.

1. I can't (see/sea) the difference.

2. She has a (ship/sheep) farm.

3. He is a (good/god) man.

4. I want to (live/leave) here.

5. She is wearing a (hat/rat).

Identify the type of assimilation in each phrase: regressive or progressive.

1. "ten pounds" → /tem paʊndz/ - Type: _______

2. "good boy" → /gʊb bɔɪ/ - Type: _______

3. "this shop" → /ðɪʃ ʃɒp/ - Type: _______

4. "cats and dogs" → /kæts ænd dɒɡz/ - Type: _______

5. "in case" → /ɪŋ keɪs/ - Type: _______

Prepare a short presentation (3-5 minutes) on one of the following topics:

  • Common pronunciation difficulties for French speakers.
  • Tips for improving English pronunciation.
  • How word stress changes the meaning of words.

Record your presentation and self-evaluate.

questions.texte: Deliver your presentation and evaluate yourself.
questions.reponse:
Example self-evaluation: 
Strengths: I used good intonation and clear word stress. Weaknesses: I struggled with the /θ/ and /ð/ sounds. I need to practice these more. I also need to work on linking words together more naturally.
